findings.message: I couldn't judge adherence because the review was given the wrong code. None of the five changed files is S001 code. They are uncommitted working-tree edits from Epic c2ba6fa6 Story s4: temporary graph-store paths in tests, and the steering refresh now asking the daemon for the repo list. The S001 corpus code is in commits a8fbd5b8..bdbb7267 under src/design/corpus/, and none of it was presented. These unrelated edits are not an S001 departure, since t6 says to preserve unrelated changes. An empty result here would therefore not mean S001 passed. Re-run the code review grounded on a8fbd5b8^..bdbb7267 (or with the unrelated working-tree changes stashed) to judge contracts.ts, canonical.ts, validate.ts and index.ts against the LLD and PLAN.
findings.expectationRef: PLAN t6: 'Diff remains within S001 modules/tests and tracked artifacts; no completion is claimed before build validation and independent code review.'

findings.message: The added store-isolation block re-imports `node:fs`, `node:os` and `node:path` under aliases (`mkdtempSyncRaw`, `rmSyncForStore`, `tmpdirForStore`, `joinForStore`), but the file already imports `mkdtempSync`, `rmSync`, `tmpdir` and `join` a few lines below. It also imports `after` from `node:test` in a separate statement next to the existing `test` import. This produces duplicate, oddly aliased imports of the same modules, which is not how these test files usually import. Merge the new names into the existing import statements.
findings.expectationRef: module-idiom: one import statement per module, no alias duplicates

findings.message: The new code adds `after` in a second `node:test` import and gives the `node:fs`/`node:os`/`node:path` names suffixed aliases (`mkdtempSyncRaw`, `joinForStore`, …). There is no name clash in this file that needs those aliases. This looks like mechanically injected boilerplate rather than the file's own import style. Fold `after` into the existing `node:test` import and use the plain names.
findings.expectationRef: module-idiom: one import statement per module, no alias duplicates

findings.message: The same 11-line temp-graph-store setup and teardown (mkdtemp → setGraphStorePath → afterAll closeGraphStore + rm) is copied word for word into three test files, each with the same comment. Test-isolation setup in this repo lives in shared files under `__tests__/helpers/` (e.g. `src/db/graph/__tests__/helpers/`). One shared helper would keep the three copies from drifting apart.
findings.expectationRef: module-idiom: shared test fixtures under __tests__/helpers

findings.message: The new `repo.list` handler passes `null as never` to `listRepos` and calls it through an inline dynamic `import()`. The other handlers in this map call statically imported functions with typed params. The `as never` cast turns off type checking of the call, so if `listRepos` starts using its argument, nothing will flag it. Prefer a static import and a typed argument, or document why the argument is unused.
findings.expectationRef: strict-optional-indexed

findings.message: The same 12-line temporary-store block (mkdtemp, setGraphStorePath, an afterAll that calls closeGraphStore and rmSync, plus four aliased imports) is pasted verbatim into three test files. If the store-isolation rule changes, for example a lance path or an env override, each copy has to be found and edited by hand. A shared helper under src/db/graph/__tests__/helpers/ (e.g. useTemporaryGraphStore()) would keep the rule in one place. The awkward import aliases (mkdtempSyncRaw, joinForStore, tmpdirForStore) also exist only to avoid name clashes in files that already import the same functions.
